Proof, not promises

Proof: a Shopify support agent our team built and tested

You shouldn't hand your customers to a system you haven't seen work. Our engineering team built a two-layer AI support agent for a Shopify-connected brand, plus an operations layer that lets it act in Shopify, the helpdesk and the 3PL. Here's how it handles four kinds of message. The orders below are synthetic.

CustomerHi, where's my order? #4417
order looked up · carrier checked
SupportIt shipped on Tuesday with UPS and it's out for delivery today. Tracking: 1Z…83. It should be with you by 8pm.
Behind the reply
  1. Router spots an order-status question and the order number.
  2. Agent reads order #4417 in Shopify, then the carrier status.
  3. Answers with the live status. No person needed.
CustomerI just ordered but put my old address. Can you change it to 22 Elm St?
order not yet fulfilled · rule allows address change
SupportDone. Order #4502 will now ship to 22 Elm St. You'll get a confirmation email in a minute.
Behind the reply
  1. Agent checks fulfilment status first.
  2. Your rule says address changes are allowed before fulfilment, so it updates Shopify.
  3. The change is written to the audit log with the conversation.
CustomerMy parcel hasn't moved in 6 days. What's going on?
carrier has no scan since label creation
SupportI can see the label was created on the 3rd, but the carrier hasn't scanned it since. I don't want to guess, so I've passed this to our team to check with the warehouse. You'll hear back today.
Behind the reply
  1. Agent looks for a scan and finds none.
  2. It doesn't make up a delivery date. It says what it knows and what it doesn't.
  3. It opens a ticket for your team with the order and tracking attached.
CustomerThe bottle arrived smashed. This is the second time. I want a refund.
damage + refund request + repeat issue → person
SupportI'm really sorry, that shouldn't happen twice. I've sent this straight to a member of our team with your order and photos. They'll sort the refund or replacement with you today.
Behind the reply
  1. Damage, refund and a repeat complaint: all three are hand-off triggers.
  2. The agent doesn't promise the refund itself.
  3. Your team gets one ticket with everything in it.
What this proves, and what it doesn't

This is engineering proof: how the system is built and how it behaves. It isn't a claim about time or money saved for a client. We publish numbers like that only once a client has let us measure them. On the audit call, we can walk you through the build itself.

For your tech team: the stack
  • Routing: Claude Haiku classifies each message. Claude Sonnet handles anything that needs reasoning or tool calls.
  • Orchestration: native Anthropic tool calling, no LangChain or third-party agent framework.
  • App: React front end, FastAPI back end, an Intercom-style support widget.
  • Operations layer: permissioned actions in Shopify (cancellations, refunds, metafields), Intercom attribute updates, fulfilment polling from the 3PL, and an audit log in BigQuery.

The demo storefront ran on SQLite with synthetic orders. In a client build, the same layers connect to your live Shopify store and helpdesk.

What it does

What AI customer service automation handles, and what it hands to your team

Most support inboxes are full of the same few questions. The answer already sits in Shopify or with the carrier. Someone just has to go and look it up.

Answered or done automatically

  • Where is my order?Live status and tracking link, pulled from the order and the carrier.
  • When will it arrive?The carrier's current estimate, plus a plain reason if it's late.
  • Can I change my address?Updated in Shopify if the order hasn't been fulfilled yet. Otherwise it explains why not.
  • Can I cancel?Cancelled within the window you set, then confirmed to the customer.
  • How do I return this?Checks eligibility against your policy and sends the return steps.
  • Product and policy questionsSizing, ingredients, shipping times, answered from your own pages.

Handed to a person, with context

  • Damaged, missing or wrong itemsPhotos and order details go to your team in one ticket.
  • Refund disputes and chargebacksNever decided by the agent.
  • Upset or repeat customersFlagged, so a person replies first.
  • Anything it can't verifyIf the data isn't there, it says so and hands over. It doesn't guess.

Your team picks up the ticket with the order, the tracking status and the full conversation already attached. Nobody has to ask the customer twice.

How it works

How the AI agent for Shopify works

It sits between your customers and your helpdesk. Your team keeps working in the tool it already uses.

  1. It reads the message

    Email, chat or WhatsApp. It works out what the customer is asking and which order they mean.

  2. It checks the real data

    The order in Shopify, the shipment with the carrier or your 3PL, and your policies.

  3. It answers or acts

    It replies, or makes a change you've allowed, like an address update before fulfilment. Every change is logged.

  4. It hands over the rest

    Exceptions go to your team in the helpdesk, with the order and the conversation attached.

FAQ

Questions about AI customer service automation

Will customers know they're talking to AI?

It can say it's an assistant, and we recommend it does. Most customers asking where their order is just want the answer quickly, and a correct answer in seconds beats a correct answer tomorrow.

What if it gives a wrong answer?

It only answers from data it can check: the order, the carrier and your policies. When the data is missing or unclear, it hands over instead of guessing. Before launch we test it on your real past tickets, and you see every reply it would have sent.

Does it work with Gorgias, Zendesk or Shopify Inbox?

Yes. You keep your helpdesk. The agent answers inside it, and handed-off tickets land in the same queue your team already works from.

What can it change in Shopify?

Only what you allow. A common starting set is address changes and cancellations before fulfilment. Refunds and anything involving money usually stay with a person. Every change is logged.

How is it priced?

A fixed price for the build and a monthly fee to keep it running and fix it when an API changes. Never per ticket or per resolution. You get the quote after the audit, once we've seen your ticket mix.

How long does it take to go live?

We usually start with a pilot on one channel and one ticket type, often order status. You get a written timeline after the audit, before you commit to anything.

Is this a fit for my store?

It's a fit if a real share of your tickets are order-status, delivery or return questions, and someone on your team spends hours a week answering them. If your volume is low, a good helpdesk setup may be enough, and we'll tell you that.

Hand the repeat questions to an agent. Keep the hard ones for your team.
